multiplechoiceresponse.p: A host at 192.168.10.20/24 wants to reach 192.168.11.5. What does it use?

choice.div: The default gateway — the target is outside its subnet.
ARP — the target is on the same subnet.
Nothing; /24 can reach any address directly.

div.p: 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.11.0/24 are different subnets, so traffic goes through the default gateway.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Why segment a network with VLANs?

choice.div: To separate traffic logically for security and performance without extra hardware.
To increase the speed of the physical switch ports.
To remove the need for IP addressing.

div.p: VLANs keep voice, data, guest, and management traffic apart while sharing the same physical switches.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which layer does DNS belong to in the TCP/IP model?

div.p: DNS is an application-layer protocol. Name resolution failing while IP connectivity works points squarely here.
